scope: Complete Round 238 manuscript diffs; written mathematical review; generated coefficient statements and elimination identities; actual-cube assembly; current proof receipts.

mathematical_review.unbounded_written_arithmetic: Valid. Permuting the coefficient triangle gives four cases by the number of entries equal to 35. Parity handles the zero case; norm bounds and divisibility handle one; the exact gcd quotients 13934,1406,1662,566 handle two; row differences and 22x=35s handle three. No bound on x,y,z is used in this written proof.
mathematical_review.bounded_Lean_arithmetic: The accepted three_coeff theorem retains all three [-9,9] bounds. These follow from the nine neighbours and ternary selection difference. The manuscript explicitly distinguishes this checked theorem from the stronger written arithmetic argument.
mathematical_review.any509_observations: Any set of 509 distinct cube positions has a complement consisting of three pairwise distinct positions. The accepted theorem allows the missing counts themselves to be zero. Its away hypothesis therefore gives exactly the stated uniqueness claim. If fewer than three positions are unobserved, extra positions can be omitted.
mathematical_review.known_parity253: A selection confined to a known parity side has zero neighbour counts at all 256 positions on that side. Adding these to 253 observed opposite-side counts gives 509 observations. This is a written specialization; no separately checked parity-specialization theorem is supplied.
mathematical_review.actual_cube: ThreeRecovery238 uses the full recursive Vertex 9, the checked inverse, antipodal diagonal and symmetry lemmas, off-diagonal coefficient membership and the automatic flipSum bounds. The binary corollary proves equality of arbitrary Boolean selections, without a snake or symmetry premise.
mathematical_review.support_range: Distinct binary selections differ in at least four neighbour counts by the theorem. A single changed vertex alters exactly nine counts. The stated range four through nine and unresolved four-missing-count question are valid.
mathematical_review.construction_scope: The new theorem proves uniqueness from count data. It does not establish binary realizability of arbitrary data, connectedness, a longer snake, or a global upper-bound improvement.
